Born José Doroteo Arango Arámbula, this guerrilla leader was a key figure in the revolution that toppled dictator Porfirio Díaz. Who is this Mexican revolutionary?
Pancho Villa: Mexican revolutionary general and politician (1878–1923)

This Confucian scholar led rebel armies against French colonial forces in 19th-century Vietnam and refused to surrender even after the French desecrated his ancestors' tombs and threatened his family — who was he?

Born a granddaughter of a Balkan king and later married to a British prince, she was widowed in 1942 when her husband died in a wartime plane crash, and spent her later years attending Commonwealth independence celebrations in Ghana and Botswana — who was this future Duchess of Kent?
Princess Marina of Greece and Denmark
Princess Marina of Greece and Denmark: Duchess of Kent (1906–1968)
Princess Marina of Greece and Denmark
At age 89 in 2023, this Spanish economist and former Communist politician was proposed as a prime ministerial candidate in a Vox-led no-confidence vote — who is he?
Ramón Tamames: Spanish economist and politician. Ramón Tamames Gómez (born 1 November 1933) is a Spanish economist and former politician.
This British lawyer-turned-diplomat was one of the architects of the League of Nations, and his lifelong defense of it earned him the 1937 Nobel Peace Prize — who was he?
Robert Cecil, Viscount Cecil of Chelwood
Robert Cecil, Viscount Cecil of Chelwood: British lawyer, politician and diplomat (1864–1958)
Robert Cecil, Viscount Cecil of Chelwood
A member of Japan's Democratic Party, this politician served in the House of Representatives of the national Diet until his death in 2018 — who is he?
The daughter of a former Arkansas governor, this politician became the third woman ever to serve as White House press secretary before winning the Arkansas governorship herself in 2022 — who is she?
Sarah Huckabee Sanders: Governor of Arkansas since 2023.
Growing out of the 19th-century Millerite movement and formally founded in 1863, this denomination observes Saturday as the Sabbath and reveres the writings of co-founder Ellen G. White — what is it?
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
Seventh-day Adventist Church: Protestant Christian denomination.
After finishing third in Turkey's 2023 presidential race, this far-right politician became a so-called kingmaker by throwing his support behind Erdoğan — who is he?

Honored with the title "Netaji," or "Respected Leader," this Indian anti-colonial figure became a hero for defying British rule — though his wartime alliances with the Axis left a troubled legacy. Who was he?
Subhas Chandra Bose: Indian nationalist leader (1897–1945)
Herodotus placed this semi-mythical harbor culture beyond the Pillars of Hercules, near the mouth of the Guadalquivir in what's now Andalusia — which Iron Age civilization?
Tartessos: Historical civilization in the southern Iberian Peninsula.
Coregent with his stepmother Hatshepsut for 22 years before ruling alone, this pharaoh led between 17 and 20 victorious military campaigns that brought Egypt's empire to its peak — who is he?
Thutmose III: Pharaoh of Egypt from 1479 to 1425 BC.

Born in Ohio and originally named Hiram, this West Point graduate led the Vicksburg campaign that seized control of the Mississippi River before becoming the Union's top general and eventually the 18th U.S. president — who is he?
Ulysses S. Grant: Civil War general, U.S. president from 1869 to 1877.
A two-time Chief Minister of Maharashtra who also served as India's Minister of Earth Sciences, this Indian National Congress politician hailed from the Latur district — who is he?
A rags-to-riches Western Han general celebrated for his campaigns against the Xiongnu, he rose through ties to Emperor Wu and was uncle to the famed general Huo Qubing — who was he?
After serving as a concubine and then empress, this woman founded her own short-lived Zhou dynasty to become the only undisputed female sovereign in China's history — who was she?
Wu Zetian: Empress regnant of China from 690 to 705.
Revered as the Father of the Nation, this ruler of Abu Dhabi became the first president of a newly unified Gulf federation in 1971?
Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan: President of the United Arab Emirates from 1971 to 2004.
Which of these people was born first?
Frank Kameny (born 1925) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four. Lovelace is often considered the first computer programmer.
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these is an astronomer?
Nancy Roman is an astronomer. Nancy Grace Roman (May 16, 1925 – December 25, 2018) was an American astronomer who made important contributions to stellar classification and stellar motions.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Omar Khayyam is a mathematician. Omar Khayyam (1048–1131) was a Persian poet and polymath, known for his contributions to mathematics, astronomy, philosophy, and Persian literature.
What is the atomic number of Iodine?
Iodine is a chemical element; it has symbol I and atomic number 53.
What is the atomic number of Cobalt?
Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.
In what year was Ken Jennings born?
Ken Jennings: Kenneth Wayne Jennings III (born May 23, 1974) is an American game show host and author who has hosted the syndicated quiz show Jeopardy! since 2021.
In what year was Valentina Tereshkova born?
Valentina Tereshkova: Valentina Vladimirovna Tereshkova (born 6 March 1937) is a Russian engineer, politician, and former Soviet cosmonaut.
In what year was Katalin Karikó born?
Katalin Karikó: Karikó laid the scientific groundwork for mRNA vaccines, overcoming major obstacles and skepticism in the scientific community.
In what year did Harold Shipman die?
Harold Shipman: Harold Frederick Shipman (14 January 1946 – 13 January 2004) was an English doctor in general practice and serial killer.
In what year did Aristotle die?
Aristotle (Ancient Greek: Ἀριστοτέλης, romanized: Aristotélēs; 384–322 BC) was an ancient Greek philosopher and polymath.
In what year was Angelman syndrome discovered?
Angelman syndrome (AS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects approximately 1 in 15,000 individuals.

Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19 (Russian: Микоян и Гуревич МиГ-19; NATO reporting name: Farmer) is a Soviet second generation, single-seat, twinjet fighter aircraft.
Yakovlev MC-21: United Aircraft Corporation. The aircraft made its maiden flight on 28 May 2017 from Irkutsk.
Which country is McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle from?

McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle: United States. The McDonnell Douglas (now Boeing) F-15E Strike Eagle is an American all-weather multirole strike fighter derived from the McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle.
Who is credited with discovering Nihonium?
Nihonium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Nihonium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Nh and atomic number 113.
Who is credited with discovering Mass–energy equivalence?
Mass–energy equivalence: Albert Einstein. In physics, mass–energy equivalence is the relationship between mass and energy in a system's rest frame.
Who is credited with discovering Plesiosaurus?
Plesiosaurus: Mary Anning. It is known by nearly complete skeletons from the Lias of England.
Which European four-engine turboprop military transport plane, sized between the Lockheed C-130 and Boeing C-17, can land on rough airstrips and double as an aerial refueling tanker?
Airbus A400M Atlas is a European four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft. It can carry heavier loads than the C-130 and can use rough landing strips.
From a Greek word meaning 'dissection,' which old branch of natural science is paired with physiology to study living things' structure and function?
Anatomy (from Ancient Greek (anatom) 'dissection') is the branch of morphology concerned with the study of the internal and external structure of organisms and their parts.
This discipline studies past human activity by recovering and analyzing artifacts, architecture, and other material remains through surveying and excavation — name the field?
Archaeology is the study of human activity through the recovery and analysis of material culture.
One of the first grains ever domesticated, this cereal crop was cultivated in the Fertile Crescent around 9000 BC and later spread throughout Eurasia by 2000 BC — name the grain?
Barley (Hordeum vulgare), a member of the grass family, is a major cereal grain grown in temperate climates globally.
Represented most commonly as a 1 or a 0, this portmanteau of 'binary digit' is the most fundamental unit of information in computing — what is it called?
Bit is the most basic unit of information in computing and digital communication.
This cabbage-family vegetable, whose large dark-green flowering head is eaten as food, closely resembles its paler relative cauliflower — name it?
Domesticated roughly 6,000 years ago in Mexico, this nightshade produces berries in red, green, and yellow ranging from mild to fiery — what is its scientific name?
Capsicum annuum is a flowering plant in the family Solanaceae (nightshades), native to the northern regions of South America and to southwestern North America.
Its other name is varicella, it spreads through the air, and it tends to hit adults harder than children — which itchy, blister-forming disease is this?
Chickenpox is a highly contagious disease caused by varicella zoster virus (VZV), a member of the herpesvirus family.

Lacking the sucking mouthparts of aphids, this chewing-mouthed insect is considered one of the most primitive alive — and a famous few of its 4,600 species became notorious household pests. What is it?
Cockroach (or roaches) are insects belonging to the order Blattodea (Blattaria).
Which compound acts as a cellular buffer and, via its phosphorylated form, hands phosphate groups back to ADP to recharge ATP in muscle and brain?
Creatine (or) is an organic compound that, in vertebrates, facilitates recycling of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), primarily in muscle and brain tissue.
Defined as having at least three loose or watery bowel movements in a day, this common condition can quickly cause dehydration, especially in children. What condition is it?
Diarrhea (American English), also spelled diarrhoea (British English), is the condition of having at least three loose, liquid, or watery bowel movements in a day.
Trained in both mathematics and philosophy, which Austrian-German thinker developed the concept of phenomenological reduction and founded a major 20th-century school of philosophy?
Edmund Husserl (Austrian; 8 April 1859 - 27 April 1938) was an Austrian-German philosopher and mathematician who established the school of phenomenology.

Discovered in January 2005 by a Palomar Observatory team and named after a Greco-Roman goddess of strife, this trans-Neptunian object is the most massive known dwarf planet in the solar system — which one?
Eris (dwarf planet) (minor-planet number 136199) is the most massive and second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
Bred in Brazil as a guard dog, cattle herder, and big-game hunter, this large mastiff-type breed was also once used to catch runaway slaves — which breed?
Fila Brasileiro (Portuguese) is a Brazilian breed of large working dog of mastiff type.
Sometimes mistakenly called the 'stomach flu' even though it's unrelated to influenza, this inflammation of the gut is usually viral, with rotavirus the top cause in children. What condition is it?
Gastroenteritis is an inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract including the stomach and intestine.
Defined as one joule of absorbed radiation energy per kilogram of matter, this SI measure is used in radiotherapy dosing and predicting acute radiation sickness — which measure is this?
Gray (unit) (symbol: Gy) is the unit of ionizing radiation dose in the International System of Units (SI), defined as the absorption of one joule of radiation energy per kilogram of matter.
This naturally occurring molecule and medication is a powerful blood anticoagulant used to treat heart attacks and prevent clotting in dialysis machines and test tubes — what is it?
Heparin (UFH), is a medication and naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan.
This endocrine condition floods the body with thyroid hormone, causing a racing heart, heat intolerance, tremor, and weight loss — and a rare 'storm' can be deadly; what is it?
Hyperthyroidism is a endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland produces excessive amounts of thyroid hormones.

From deep-sea gribbles to the woodlice under your garden stones, members of this crustacean order share seven pairs of jointed limbs and brood their young in a pouch called a marsupium — what is the order?
Isopoda is an order of crustaceans. The order is divided into eleven suborders.
This Confederate veteran and pharmacist sold the rights to his 1886 beverage recipe to Asa Griggs Candler for about $2,300 shortly before he died — who is he?
John Stith Pemberton (July 8, 1831 - August 16, 1888) was an American pharmacist, chemist, and Confederate States Army officer who is best known as the inventor of Coca-Cola.
When the natural curve of the thoracic spine exceeds about 45 degrees, doctors give this excessive rounding of the upper back a name rooted in the Greek word for 'hump' — what is it?
Kyphosis (from Greek (kyphos) 'hump') is an abnormally excessive convex curvature of the spine as it occurs in the thoracic and sacral regions.
Sociable for a big cat and more active by day than its relatives, this savannah hunter is so sexually dimorphic that only the males grow a sweeping mane. Which animal?
Lion (Panthera leo) is a large cat of the genus Panthera, currently ranging only in Sub-Saharan Africa and India.

This German sexologist founded the Scientific-Humanitarian Committee, which carried out what's been called the first advocacy for homosexual and transgender rights — before the Nazis stripped his citizenship in 1933. Who was he?
Magnus Hirschfeld (14 May 1868 - 14 May 1935) was a German physician, sexologist, and LGBTQ advocate whose German citizenship was revoked in 1933 by the Nazi government.
First isolated from a cow's pineal gland in 1958 because it could lighten the skin of frogs, this nighttime hormone went on to become famous for governing the sleep-wake cycle — what is it?
Melatonin is a natural compound produced by various organisms, including bacteria and eukaryotes.
This small, subterranean mammal has velvety fur, tiny eyes, and short powerful forelimbs with oversized paws built for constant digging — what animal is it?

It's the inherent character of the universe as a whole — the laws, elements, and phenomena of the physical world, including life itself — even though humans are often spoken of as somehow apart from it. What is it?
Nature is an inherent character or constitution, particularly of the ecosphere or the universe as a whole.
This family of three long, ribbon-like pelagic fish species includes the longest bony fish alive, stretching up to about 8 meters, yet rarely seen by humans — what fish is it?
Oarfish are the three species of large and extremely long pelagic lampriform fish belonging to the small family Regalecidae.
Its name comes from the Greek for "from everywhere" because it turns up in nearly all foods — and this B vitamin lets animals build coenzyme A for energy. Which vitamin is it?
Pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) is a B vitamin and an essential nutrient.
This Belgian-British microbiologist helped discover the Ebola virus in 1976 and led the fight against that first recorded outbreak before becoming a pioneering AIDS researcher — who is he?
Peter Piot (born 17 February 1949) is a Belgian-British microbiologist known for his research into Ebola and AIDS.
Which silvery-white precious metal carries the symbol Pt, leads group 10 of the periodic table, and is far rarer in Earth's crust than its glittering cousins?
Platinum is a chemical element; it has symbol Pt and atomic number 78.
This viscous, nearly odorless liquid with a faintly sweet taste is classified as a diol and is approved by the FDA as a safe food additive — what compound is it?
Propylene glycol (IUPAC name: propane-1,2-diol) is a viscous, colorless liquid.
This German centre-back developed through Hertha BSC's youth ranks before winning many honors at Bayern Munich, following a season at Manchester City. Who is he?
Rattus is a genus of muroid rodents, all typically called rats.

Known by folk names like knotberry and lowbush salmonberry, this amber fruit structurally similar to a blackberry thrives in Arctic tundra and boreal forest but isn't farmed commercially — which species?
Rubus chamaemorus (also known as cloudberry) is a species of flowering plant in the rose family, Rosaceae.
Most episodes of this brain-activity disruption last under two minutes and leave the person confused or fatigued afterward, but one lasting over five minutes is a medical emergency — what is it?
Seizure is a sudden disruption of brain activity caused by excessive, synchronized neuronal firing that results in changes in behavior.
With symbol Na from the Neo-Latin 'natrium' and a single stable isotope, this reactive metal sits in group 1 and is found in minerals like halite and feldspar — what is it?
Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
A small Eurasian mustelid that turns brilliant white in winter, this animal's coat — known as ermine — once draped Catholic monarchs and the Infant Jesus of Prague — what is it?
Stoat (Mustela erminea), also known as the Eurasian ermine or ermine, is a species of mustelid native to Eurasia and the northern regions of North America.
A mathematics prodigy who abandoned academia in 1969 for a reclusive primitive life, he later mailed bombs over 17 years and penned a 35,000-word manifesto against modern technology — who was he?
Ted Kaczynski (k-; May 22, 1942 - June 10, 2023), also known as the Unabomber, was an American mathematician and domestic terrorist.
This metric unit of mass equals exactly 1,000 kilograms — about 2,204.6 pounds — and is technically identical to the SI unit called the megagram. What is it?
Tonne (or; symbol: t) is a unit of mass equal to 1,000 kilograms.
At just 26, this Soviet cosmonaut became the first woman in space, orbiting Earth 48 times solo aboard Vostok 6 in 1963. Who is she?
Valentina Tereshkova (born 6 March 1937) is a Russian engineer, politician, and former Soviet cosmonaut.

Dubbed the "father of English geology," this man created the first detailed geological map of an entire country — yet his humble background got him snubbed by scientists and even landed him in debtors' prison. Who was he?
William Smith (geologist) (23 March 1769 - 28 August 1839) was an English geologist, credited with creating the first detailed, nationwide geological map of any country.
A legendary Heian-era court diviner and astrologer, this figure lived 84 years free of illness, fueling belief in mystical powers — a Kyoto shrine bears his name today. Who is he?
A shortened-fuselage version of a popular narrow-body jetliner family, this aircraft entered service with Swissair in April 1996 and carries up to 156 passengers — which model?
Airbus A319: Airliner, shortened variant of the A320 family.
Sold under the brand name Xanax, this fast-acting benzodiazepine is most often prescribed for panic disorder and generalized anxiety — what drug is it?
Alprazolam: Benzodiazepine medication. Alprazolam is most commonly prescribed in the management of anxiety disorders, especially panic disorder and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD).
Commonly called windflowers, which genus of the buttercup family is native to every continent except Australia, New Zealand, and Antarctica?
Anemone: Genus of flowering plants in the family Ranunculaceae.
Named for a mythological weaver transformed into a spider, which eight-legged class of arthropods includes scorpions, ticks, and mites?
Arachnid: Class of arthropods. The term is derived from the Greek word ἀράχνη (aráchnē, 'spider'), from the myth of the hubristic human weaver Arachne, who was turned into a spider.
Driven by elevated LDL cholesterol, this chronic inflammatory disease builds plaque lesions inside artery walls and can lead to stroke or coronary trouble — what is it?
Atherosclerosis: Inflammatory disease involving a buildup of lesions in the walls of arteries.
The only mammals capable of true sustained flight, this group flies on long digits webbed with a thin membrane and makes up about 20% of all classified mammals — what are they?

Named after two French physicists who discovered it in 1820, this equation in magnetostatics relates a magnetic field to the strength, direction, and distance of an electric current — which physics rule?
Biot–Savart law: Law of classical electromagnetism.

Completely dependent on humans for reproduction after millennia of selective breeding, this domesticated moth's caterpillars produce the raw fiber behind a 5,000-year-old Chinese industry — which species?
Bombyx mori: Moth mainly used in the production of silk.

Prescribed under the tongue, as a cheek film, an injection, a skin patch, or an implant, this opioid treats pain and opioid use disorder — often combined with naloxone in Suboxone to deter injection misuse. What is it?
Buprenorphine: Opioid used to treat pain and opioid use disorder.
Called 'rockmelon' in Australia and 'spanspek' in South Africa, this orange-fleshed true melon goes by yet another name in North America — what fruit is it?
Cantaloupe: Variety of melon. Originally, cantaloup referred to the true cantaloupe or European cantaloupe with non- to slightly netted and often ribbed rind.
Sold under the brand name Rocephin, this injectable third-generation antibiotic treats everything from meningitis to gonorrhea — which drug?
Ceftriaxone: Antibiotic medication. Ceftriaxone, sold under the brand name Rocephin, is a third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic used for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
The only member of the onion genus native to both the New World and Old World, this perennial herb has edible leaves and flowers and doubles as a natural insect repellent — what is it?
Chives: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
With a coat of dusky-grey blotches that inspired its common name, this wild cat is one of the few able to climb down tree trunks head-first, using a long tail for balance — what species is it?

Clouded leopard: Species of wild cat. Its head-and-body length ranges from 68.6 to 108 cm (27.0 to 42.5 in) with a 61 to 91 cm (24 to 36 in) long tail, which it uses for balancing when moving in trees.
Often defined as the transmission of information, this concept is famously modeled as a source encoding a message, sending it through a channel, and a receiver decoding it — what is it?
Communication: Transmission of information. Models of communication are simplified overviews of its main components and their interactions.
Unknown in the wild, this cultivated autumn-flowering plant has had its dried stigmas prized as the world's priciest spice for over 3,500 years — what is its scientific name?
Crocus sativus: Species of flowering plant. Crocus sativus, commonly known as saffron crocus or autumn crocus, is a species of flowering plant in the iris family Iridaceae.
Introduced in 1984, this turboprop regional airliner series was developed from an earlier company model and later gained 'Quiet' variants with active noise-cancellation — which aircraft family?

De Havilland Canada Dash 8: Canadian turboprop airliner. The De Havilland Canada DHC-8, commonly known as the Dash 8, is a series of turboprop-powered regional airliners, introduced by de Havilland Canada (DHC) in 1984.

The largest collection of fossils from this extinct Ice Age canine came from the La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles, though it roamed from South American savanna to North American forested mountains — what animal was it?
Dire wolf: Extinct species of canine mammal.
Its name comes from the Greek word for 'house,' and it studies organisms from the level of a single individual all the way up to the entire biosphere — which branch of biology is it?
Ecology: Study of organisms and their environment.
This branch of zoology, whose name derives from Greek words for 'insect' and 'study,' covers a field that has described over 1.3 million species — which discipline?
The only Old World member of its family to breed in the Northern Hemisphere's temperate zones, this migratory songbird winters in central and southern Africa — what is it?
Eurasian golden oriole: Species of bird.

An annual legume with leaves of three small leaflets, this semiarid crop has flavored dishes of the Indian subcontinent since ancient times — yet there's little clinical proof it works as the supplement people often take. What is it?
Named for the mathematician who used it to solve the heat equation, this expansion writes a periodic function as an infinite sum of sines and cosines — what is it?
Fourier series: Decomposition of periodic functions.
This field studies the relationship between food and culture, encompassing everything from cooking techniques and regional cuisines to the science of good eating — what is it called?

Gastronomy: Study of the relationship between food and culture. One who is well versed in gastronomy is called a gastronome, while a gastronomist is one who unites theory and practice in the study of gastronomy.
The most abundant free amino acid in human blood, this one is named after the compound found in gluten and is coded for by the codons CAA and CAG — what is it?
Glutamine: Amino acid. Glutamine (symbol Gln or Q) is an α-amino acid that is used in the biosynthesis of proteins.

Beginning as weakness in the feet and hands before spreading upward, this rapid-onset autoimmune condition attacks the peripheral nervous system and can require a ventilator in about 15% of cases — which disorder is this?
Guillain–Barré syndrome: Autoimmune disease. Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS) is a rapid-onset muscle weakness caused by the immune system damaging the peripheral nervous system.
Tapeworms, flukes and roundworms all fall under this broad name for any infection where parasitic worms take up residence in the body. What is the condition called?
Helminthiasis: Any macroparasitic disease caused by helminths.
Belonging to the genus Apis, this eusocial insect builds perennial nests of hexagonal wax cells and stores surplus food as a prized sweet — which creature is it?
This condition, caused by low blood potassium below 3.5 mmol/L, can bring on fatigue, leg cramps, and a dangerously slow heart rhythm — what is it?
Hypokalemia: Insufficient potassium in the blood. Normal potassium levels in humans are between 3.5 and 5.0 mmol/L (3.5 and 5.0 mEq/L) with levels below 3.5 mmol/L defined as hypokalemia.
Discovered by Bernard Courtois in 1811, this heaviest stable halogen melts to a deep violet liquid and is the heaviest essential nutrient — needed to make thyroid hormones. What element is it?
Iodine: Chemical element with atomic number 53 (I)
Enlisting disguised as a man named 'Jean' on Bougainville's expedition, this expert botanist became the first woman to circumnavigate the globe — who is she?
Jeanne Baret: French explorer, naturalist, botanist (1740–1807)

This Indian aerospace engineer led the nation's space agency as chairman and served as secretary of the Department of Space, after directing both the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre and the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre — who is he?
What is this — “Parts of the vulva”?
Labia: Parts of the vulva. The labia are the major externally visible structures of the vulva.
Used to treat everything from pneumonia to Legionnaires' disease, this broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic is the left-handed mirror-image isomer of a drug called ofloxacin — what is it?
Levofloxacin: Antibiotic. Levofloxacin, sold under the brand name Levaquin among others, is a broad-spectrum antibiotic of the fluoroquinolone drug class.
Sometimes called the Japanese medlar or Japanese plum, this evergreen tree from the hills of south-central China produces small orange fruit — which plant?
Loquat: Species of plant. The loquat (Eriobotrya japonica, Chinese: 枇杷; Pinyin: pípá) is a large evergreen shrub or tree grown commercially for its orange coloured fruits.
Genetically related to the Bichon, Bolognese, and Havanese, this toy breed sports a silky white coat, doesn't shed, and tops out around 4 kilograms — what breed is it?
Maltese dog: Breed of toy dog. The precise link, if any, between the modern and ancient breeds is not known.

Entering US Navy service in 1961 before the Marines and Air Force adopted it too, this twin-engine supersonic jet became America's most-produced supersonic military aircraft with 5,195 built — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II: Fighter aircraft family developed from 1958.
Sold as Flagyl, this antibiotic and antiprotozoal fights everything from giardiasis to trichomoniasis — but it's notorious for leaving a metallic taste in your mouth — what is it?
Metronidazole: Antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication. Metronidazole, sold under the brand name Flagyl and Metrogyl among others, is an antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication.
Its dust-like, colored, fuzzy appearance on food comes from spores, and its branching network of hyphae — called a mycelium — counts as a single organism; what fungal structure is this?
Mold: Wooly, dust-like fungal structure or substance.
One of the smallest self-replicating organisms known, this cell-wall-lacking bacterium was originally called the 'Eaton agent' after being cultivated in chicken eggs in 1944 — what organism is it?
Mycoplasma pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a species of very small-cell bacteria that lack a cell wall, in the class Mollicutes.
This British-American historian, a senior fellow at Stanford's Hoover Institution, writes on financial history and holds notably favorable views of the British Empire — who is he?
Weighing up to 1,000 kg and resembling a fish head without a tail, this giant marine creature can be as tall as it is long when its fins are extended — what is it?
Ocean sunfish: Species of fish. The ocean sunfish (Mola mola), also known as the common mola, is one of the largest bony fish in the world.
This paired female gonad releases egg cells and secretes hormones that regulate the menstrual cycle and fertility — which organ?
Ovary: Female reproductive organ that produces egg cells.
Best known for creating Gmail, this engineer also built the first prototype of Google's ad platform and once suggested the company's old motto, 'Don't be evil' — who is he?
Native to Eurasia but now introduced worldwide, this game bird has been flagged in the UK as a threat to endangered native adders — what is it?
Members of this eukaryotic kingdom mostly make their own food with chlorophyll, though parasitic kinds have ditched photosynthesis entirely to feed off others — what kingdom is it?
Plant: Kingdom of organisms. Historically, as in Aristotle's biology, the plant kingdom encompassed all living things that were not animals, and included algae and fungi.
This corticosteroid treats conditions from rheumatoid arthritis to asthma but can cause bone loss and psychiatric side effects with long-term use — what is it called?
Prednisolone: Corticosteroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a vein, used topically as a skin cream, or as eye drops.
Excess fluid pooling in the lungs' air sacs impairs oxygen exchange and can be triggered by either heart failure or a range of unrelated causes — what condition is this?
Pulmonary edema: Fluid accumulation in the tissue and air spaces of the lungs.
Domesticated roughly 8,000 years ago, this Southeast Asian bird species is the primary wild ancestor of today's chickens — which bird?
Red junglefowl: Species of bird; ancestor of the chicken. The red junglefowl was the primary species to give rise to today's many breeds of chicken (G. g. domesticus).
Nicknamed the 'Bone,' this variable-sweep-wing heavy bomber was dreamed up to fuse the B-58's Mach 2 speed with the B-52's range and payload — which aircraft is it?
Rockwell B-1 Lancer: American strategic bomber.
This business magnate founded the world's largest retailer by revenue in 1962, was the richest person in America throughout the 1980s, and left behind the country's wealthiest family — who is he?
Rising from general secretary in 1981 to FIFA's eighth president in 1998, this Swiss administrator won re-election four times before being suspended in the 2015 corruption scandal — who is he?
Found from Bangladesh to the Philippines, these nocturnal primates make up the genus Nycticebus and include at least eight recognized species — what are they called?
